name: Malpedia lookup
description: Search and expand Malpedia family, actor and sample metadata using existing MISP objects.

routing.text, other: Canonical family IDs such as win.emotet use get/family directly. Other values search both family and actor names/aliases.
routing.malware-type: Search family names and aliases, or expand a canonical family ID directly.
routing.threat-actor: Search actor names and synonyms, then expand matching actor records and their embedded families.
routing.link, url: Accept only Malpedia /details/<family_id> and /actor/<actor_id> URLs. Retrieve their records directly.
routing.md5, sha256, filename|md5, filename|sha2: Query get/sample/<hash>/info using an API token, then expand the reported family. SHA-1 is not supported by this API.

apikey.description: Optional API token sent as Authorization: apitoken <token>. Required for sample hash queries. Public family/actor queries work without a token.

max_results.description: Limit per family/actor search, embedded actor family collection, and YARA file collection. YARA lookups are also limited to this many distinct families per invocation. Truncation is recorded in result comments.

include_yara.description: Retrieve family YARA files, preserving complete source and license metadata. API sharing levels become TLP tags on every attribute of the YARA object. Accepts booleans and true/false/1/0 strings.

output_mapping.family: malware object: common_name -> name, alt_names and canonical family ID -> alias, description -> description, is_family=true.
output_mapping.actor: intrusion-set object: value -> name, meta.synonyms and canonical actor ID -> aliases, description -> description. Actor uses references point to its embedded malware families.
output_mapping.sample: file object: md5 and sha256 -> hash attributes; belongs-to reference to the expanded family.
output_mapping.yara: yara object: complete rule file -> yara, family page -> reference; detects reference to malware object. Each returned file remains intact, even if it contains multiple rules.
output_mapping.references: Deduplicated link attributes reached by described-by object references. These are reference reports, not malicious URLs.
output_mapping.attribution: Deduplicated threat-actor attributes reached by attributed-to references from malware objects. Attribution labels are preserved without resolving them to additional actor identities.
output_mapping.other_metadata: Notes, timestamps, source IDs, external UUIDs, actor country and other unmapped metadata are retained as JSON in object comments. Malpedia cluster UUIDs are not reused as object UUIDs.
output_mapping.input: The original attribute UUID, tags, comment and detection flag are retained. Objects reference the original attribute. All generated attributes have to_ids=false.

behavior: Missing settings, JSON null and empty strings use the documented defaults. Other invalid values, including zero or boolean integer settings, are rejected.
Exact identifier, name and alias search matches take priority; otherwise return the first max_results substring matches in API order.
Related families are deduplicated by canonical ID, including families shared by multiple actors.
Primary lookup failures return an error. Optional YARA and sample-to-family enrichment failures preserve successful results with an explanatory object comment.
Requests use HTTPS with certificate validation, a timeout and no redirects. Only read-only GET endpoints are used; no malware binaries are downloaded or submitted.
installation: Copy misp_modules/modules/expansion/malpedia.py into the same path in your misp-modules checkout. No registration or extra Python dependency is needed beyond requests and PyMISP.
Restart your misp-modules service. In MISP, enable Plugin.Enrichment_malpedia_enabled and set Plugin.Enrichment_malpedia_apikey if required. Configure the other exposed module settings as needed.
Existing malware, intrusion-set, file and yara templates suffice; no misp-objects change or custom template installation is required.

validation.live: Public family, alias search, actor and YARA endpoints checked against Malpedia. Authenticated sample-info success is covered by mocked records only: no Malpedia API token was available.
